src: Fine-needle aspiration of the left thyroid nodule was reported as Bethesda category V, suspicious for malignancy.
The tumour is a papillary thyroid carcinoma, tall cell subtype, with minimal extrathyroidal extension and metastases in level VI lymph nodes.

src: Nuclear features include enlargement, overlapping, nuclear grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions; psammoma bodies are present.
This encapsulated follicular-patterned lesion without capsular or vascular invasion qualifies as NIFTP rather than carcinoma.
The background thyroid shows Hashimoto thyroiditis with lymphoid follicles, germinal centres and Hurthle cell change.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma was suspected because of a raised serum calcitonin, and a germline RET mutation was found.
The patient underwent total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection, followed by radioactive iodine therapy.

src: Multinodular goitre with abundant colloid and cystic degeneration; there is no evidence of malignancy.
Frozen section showed a follicular neoplasm; the final diagnosis was minimally invasive follicular carcinoma.
Primary hyperparathyroidism was caused by a single parathyroid adenoma; the remaining glands showed no hyperplasia.
The adrenal cortical carcinoma met five Weiss criteria, including necrosis and atypical mitoses.
Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma are positive for chromogranin A and synaptophysin.
The pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET) was of PIT1 lineage, with a Ki-67 index of 4%.

src: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours are graded by mitotic count and Ki-67 index.
A hypoechoic, taller-than-wide nodule with microcalcifications was classified as ACR TI-RADS 5.
